metric.semantic_determinacy.basis_disclosure: This figure is computed on Kotlin's own all-fragments basis (41 of 44 probes; n_L = 41), NOT yet on the cross-language common basis defined in capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics (probes for which ALL TEN languages have a fragment). The runner must recompute the common-basis figure once all ten languages' shards are merged, restricting the probe set to the intersection and re-deriving mean(log2(B_i)) and the normalized score over that intersection; this worker's per-probe B_i table is the raw input required for that merge.

excluded_none_probes.reason: N-1: Kotlin/JVM under the frozen recipe (kotlinc ... -include-runtime; java -jar) has no built-in FFI mechanism to call a native C function without a separate native-compilation/JNI step or an out-of-toolchain FFM API, which R7/toolchain_binding disallow as third-party/extra-toolchain.

metric.semantic_determinacy.limitations: B_i values above are this worker's documented judgement applying the frozen branching definition (materially different interpretations of mutation/aliasing/failure/conversion/dispatch/resource/control-flow/representation/result compatible with the local surface form alone) to Kotlin's actual language and stdlib rules, cross-checked against Kotlin language documentation conventions (val/var, sealed classes, List vs MutableList, Elvis operator, safe calls, AtomicLong, use{}). No fragment was executed in a live toolchain within this packet-only worker; V1 (build/run verification) evidence must be supplied by a build-executing worker and reconciled with this determinacy table before final publication.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_ref: semantic_compression.md section B (Semantic Determinacy), capability_universe.json probes, semantic_site_matrix.json
metric.semantic_determinacy.normalization_note: Spec 6.1.3.B fixes the raw measure and its direction (lower branching better) but does not itself fix a 0-100 transform. This worker applies a documented, mechanically reproducible transform so the runner's 0-100/100-best convention holds: geometric_mean_B = 2^mean(log2(B_i)); normalized_score = min(100, 100 / geometric_mean_B). A fully determinate fragment set (all B_i = 1) yields geometric_mean_B = 1 and a normalized score of 100. This transform is applied identically to every language's own B_i data and does not depend on any other language's results.

per_probe_branching.rationale: val n = 7; return n -- val is unambiguously immutable, initialized, Int-typed from local form alone.
var counter: Long = 0 (mutable) vs const val LIMIT: Long = 100 (compile-time constant) -- var/const val keywords are unambiguous locally.
var v: Int declared without initializer; Kotlin's definite-assignment analysis statically guarantees v is assigned on every path before the final read; only one compiled interpretation is possible.
Kotlin has no way to obtain genuinely uninitialized bulk storage; substituted ByteArray(16), which is documented to be zero-initialized deterministically (R9 substitution, P-a).
x += 1 on Int is in-place, wraps silently on overflow per JVM Int semantics; a single defined outcome.
xs[1] = 42 on a MutableList invokes set() in place; unambiguous.

val window: List<Int> = xs -- surface form alone does not distinguish a copying view from a non-copying reference-typed view without knowledge of Kotlin's List/MutableList reference semantics; 2 interpretations remain locally plausible (copy vs shared view).
first === second uses Kotlin's dedicated referential-equality operator, unambiguous identity test.

Bare call f(x) with no sigil: per the probe's own binding enumeration, all 6 listed outcomes (no access / read-only / write elements / replace-resize / retain alias / copy made) remain compatible with Kotlin's plain call-site syntax alone, since Kotlin gives no call-site marker distinguishing them.
val neg = { a: Int -> k - a }; xs.map(neg) -- lambda capture and application are unambiguous.
Int is a value type on the JVM; a returned Int is always an independent value copy, never a shared reference -- single interpretation.
Pair<Int,Int> destructured via val (q, r) = divmod2(a, b); standard, unambiguous.
a * b + c on Int -- fixed precedence and fixed (wrapping) overflow behavior, single interpretation.
Int / Int truncates, % follows dividend sign, toDouble() is the sole explicit widening form Kotlin provides; no operator ambiguity.
m + 1 at Int.MAX_VALUE wraps silently (no standard checked/saturating Int add in Kotlin stdlib); single defined outcome (rung iv).
Explicit guard on b == 0 substituting 0 (rung ii, no standard checked-division optional in Kotlin); unambiguous.
s1 == s2 on String always calls equals() (content comparison) in Kotlin, never identity; single interpretation.
xs.sortedDescending() (non-mutating, new list) vs sortDescending() (mutating) are distinctly named; chosen form is unambiguous once selected.
big.toInt() truncates to low 32 bits silently; single defined JVM/Kotlin outcome (rung ii/iii, no standard checked narrowing).
i + d resolves via Kotlin's defined Int.plus(Double): Double operator overload; single result type, no silent implicit-conversion ambiguity.
xs[i] on List throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range; single defined outcome.

xs.subList(1, 4) -- surface form alone does not reveal whether the returned List copies or shares backing storage without consulting List/MutableList documentation; 2 locally plausible interpretations.
var o: Int? = null; val n = o ?: 0 -- Elvis operator is unambiguous fallback.
o?.let(h) -- safe-call short-circuits on null deterministically; single interpretation.

Kotlin has no checked exceptions and no throws annotation requirement; the bare declared signature of parse_twice is compatible with two interpretations locally -- 'cannot fail' and 'may throw an unchecked exception' -- without consulting the body or documentation.
Explicit try { s.toInt() } catch (e: NumberFormatException) { 0 } -- protected scope and fallback are locally explicit.
sealed class Shape with data class Circle/Rect subtypes is a closed set enforced by the compiler; unambiguous.
when (s) over a sealed class is compiler-checked exhaustive with no else arm permitted to be omitted silently; single interpretation of coverage guarantee.
interface Shape { fun area(): Double } implemented by Circle/Rect in one unit and by Tri in a separate unit; ordinary virtual dispatch, unambiguous.
fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T -- static type relationship between argument and result is preserved by Kotlin's type system at each call site; unambiguous.
fun <T : Comparable<T>> maxOf(a: T, b: T): T -- declaration-site bound, checked at declaration; unambiguous.
List<Named> holding A() and B(); items[0].tag() dispatches virtually; unambiguous.
mutableListOf(1,2,3).sum() -- standard stdlib reduction, unambiguous.

mapOf(...) returns a Map; the Map interface contract itself does not guarantee iteration order even though the concrete LinkedHashMap-backed implementation Kotlin actually returns preserves insertion order -- 2 locally plausible interpretations (ordered vs unordered) without consulting implementation notes.
File(...).bufferedReader().use { ... } guarantees close() on every exit path including exceptions (Closeable + use{}); unambiguous.
Kotlin has no deterministic finalizer; substituted an explicit AutoCloseable Handle invoked via use{} (P-a), which deterministically runs cleanup exactly once at scope exit.
println("x") is available without any import; unambiguous.
object Util { fun pub_add(...); private fun secret() } -- private enforced at compile time across files; unambiguous.
Two java.lang.Thread instances (JVM standard runtime bundled with Kotlin's frozen recipe) computing 20 and 22, joined, summed; unambiguous.
java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong.incrementAndGet() from two threads is documented atomic/race-free; unambiguous.

metric.semantic_determinacy.probe_basis: 41 of the 44 frozen probes are supported (FULL or PARTIAL) for Kotlin under the frozen toolchain recipe and therefore enter this raw computation. 3 probes are scored NONE for Kotlin and are excluded from this determinacy computation (per spec 6.1.7 interaction_with_quality_metrics, metrics A-D are computed on fragments that exist; NONE probes have no fragment to measure branching on). Excluded probes and reasons are listed below; their absence is captured instead by Capability Coverage (metric C), not by this metric.
metric.semantic_determinacy.raw_measure_definition: For each fixed probe i, B_i = count of materially different semantic interpretations (mutation, aliasing, failure, conversion, dispatch, resource behavior, control flow, representation, or observable result) compatible with the probe's LOCAL surface form alone, before consulting external declarations/whole-program facts. Raw metric per spec 6.1.3.B is mean(log2(B_i)) over probes with a fragment (FULL or PARTIAL support); lower is better.
